Lassen County Superior Court

Address: 2610 Riverside Dr, Susanville, CA 96130

Phone: +15302518205

Lassen County Superior Court is a city courthouse serving the residents of Lassen County, California. It is located within the court of appeal in the third district, and the request from the eastern state district goes to the ninth circuit United State Court of appeal. The courthouse was established in 1864 but was dismissed and replaced by a superior court system in 1880. A new justice courthouse was established in 1917 then in 2012, all the operations and court divisions were shifted to a new hall of justice. The court's mission is to verify the rule of law by giving fair justice, and to protect the rights and liberties of the people according to the constitution of the State of California and the constitution of the United States of America. It has jurisdiction over criminal, civil, family, juvenile, traffic, and vehicle matters. They provide services like online payment, case index, calendar portal forms, fines, and many more, so it is optional to go to court for these services. This court also provides self-help for a different division. Live chats with the clerk court are also available. Proper dressing is required during the court session. Please do not bring any illegal weapon into the courthouse because it is unlawful, and the law enforcement officer will scan you when you enter the court. One superior court located in this county is:

How to search for case information?

Lassen County Superior Court Case Search can be done online using the court portal https://cms.lassencourt.ca.gov/. The court maintained all the case records in the file or database. The case search can be done in the following ways:

  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by party name
  • Searching by first and last name
  • Searching by citation or ticket number
  • Searching by previous case number

After you enter any search information, it will come if it is available and is not confidential and sealed. If the case is personal and sealed, then you have to go to the court and request record access, and then the court will decide whether to provide that case information or not.

How can I request copies of the records?

Lassen County Superior Court records contain information on all the cases. The copies are available in the court. Suppose you want confidential information that is not available online. In that case, you can access them by visiting the court, making the request, and viewing a file by bringing a filled-out LSC-MIS-100, Research and Copy Request Form along with a valid driver's license or another valid photo I.D. to the Hall of Justice. If you want copies of records, you can request them online via https://www.lassencourt.ca.gov/general_info/research-copy-request-eform.shtml, visit the hall of justice or mail the form to the court mailing address. Fees per page are required for each record copy.

How to make a payment?

Lassen County Superior Court payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person:

A person can pay tickets and fines by visiting the hall of justice during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, U.S. funds, or a card at the court payment office. Take your ticket and case number with you when you come for payment. 2% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online:

Online payments can be made using the court online portal https://www.lassencourt.ca.gov/online_services/makepay-online.shtml. Select your payment type, like you want to pay for a case/ traffic ticket or research and copy request payment. Convenience fees will be applied using this method.

Mail:

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address, "Lassen Superior Court," to 2610 Riverside Drive • Susanville, CA 96130. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number, and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt. If you are paying for a traffic ticket, please attach the courtesy notice to the envelope.

Phone:

A person can make payment by calling 530-251-8205 and following all the instructions that they said. Service charges will be applied in this case.

How to appear remotely?

Lassen County Superior Court remote appearances for some eligible cases are possible using audio by telephone with charges and video conferencing using zoom without any payments. Select the option of your choice of remote hearing. If you want an audio hearing, follow all the instructions https://www.lassencourt.ca.gov/online_services/telephonicappearance.shtml while if you wish to video conference via zoom, then view the education at https://www.lassencourt.ca.gov/online_services/zoomappearance.shtml. In zoom, appearance makes sure your internet connection is strong. Mute your microphone and speak only when the judge calls your name. Test your microphone and video before joining the session. It is recommended to avoid running unnecessary applications when you are in a meeting. Wear a proper dress and sit where your face is visible. Recording in video conferencing is strictly prohibited; if you do it, it will result in the imposition of sanctions.

The family law division handles which types of cases?

Lassen County Court Family law division handles matters related to family issues, the relationship between couples and many other matters. These issues include:

  • Divorce, legal separation and nullity
  • Child custody, visitation and support or support action
  • Family or spousal support
  • Domestic violence issue
  • Division of marital property

The division also provides the family law facilitators' service at no cost to those who cannot afford an attorney or lawyer. You only had to pay for the filing form. They provide assistance in obtaining the order for child custody, support or spousal support, give computerized child or spousal support calculations, and offer mediation in a child or spousal health insurance.

What is the purpose of family court services?

Lassen County Family Court provides mediation services on some divorce or legal separations where the parents disagree on the sharing plan of child custody. The purpose of the family court service is to:

  • Assist in the domestic controversies settlements involving the children's welfare.
  • Try to guarantee that the children get equal contact with both parents at the end of a marriage.
  • Encourage parents to take responsibility and cooperate for the betterment of children.

How many types of juvenile cases are handled by this court?

Lassen County juvenile court handles the cases in which a minor is involved. Two types of cases are taken that are:

· Juvenile delinquency cases:

It includes cases in which a juvenile violates the rules and is charged with violating the law, and it is considered a crime if an adult commits it. The child's further responsibility and placement will be given to the child probation department.

· Juvenile dependency cases:

It involves a case in which the juvenile is neglected or abused. The child's further responsibility and placement will be given to the child protective service.

Juvenile cases are confidential, and the data is only provided to the person involved, like the parents, attorney and lawyer.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

Lassen County traffic court handles traffic and vehicle violations that include speeding, driving without or with an expired license, driving while you have drugs, accidents etc. The court will mail you a courtesy notice on the citation address after you receive a traffic or infraction ticket. That notice will tell you detailed information on the citation number, schedule, violation you had done, bail amount, eligibility for traffic violation school etc. If your citation includes a court appearance, then appearing in the court on the schedule is mandatory. Many options for resolving traffic tickets if a court appearance is not required are:

  • Sign up for the traffic school if your case is eligible. After completing it, your traffic infraction records will be removed.
  • Pay the total amount of the fine on time
  • Show some proof of correction if the case is related to insurance or no vehicle registration and pay a reduced amount of fine with the correction fees.
  • Contest the violation by requesting a trial by sending a plea of not guilty. Two types of trials are available: written declaration trials and trials by the court.

You had to respond with a solution before the deadline. Contact the clerk's office if you are still waiting to receive any mail for courtesy notice.

FAQ:

Which things I had to bring when coming for family facilitators?

When reaching for the family facilitator's service, you must get your income or expense information, last three pay stubs, and last tax return income statement.

What happens if I fail to appear or pay after the deadline is passed?

If you do not pay the fine or do not appear on the schedule, then a misdemeanor charge with $260 penalties will be applied to you, an arrest warrant will be issued against you, a civil assessment of $100 will be imposed upon you, your driving license and insurance will be suspended
